title: Measure error
description: Error body from POST /measure (and, once TICK-225 lands, every other path on this service). Frozen by TICK-224 so TICK-063 can code against failure as well as success. HTTP status is not a field in the body; it is paired with this shape as follows: 400 — the request is missing a required part or the sidecar is not JSON; 422 — the sidecar is JSON but fails capture_sidecar.schema.json. This SUPERSEDES TICK-060 AC4, which specified 400 for a schema-invalid sidecar; 422 distinguishes a well-formed request carrying bad content from a malformed request, which TICK-063 needs in order to tell the operator whether to re-capture or re-send. Free to change now because no client consumes it yet. TICK-225 (#113) landed: every response from this service now carries this shape, including statuses raised before any view runs — 404 (unknown path), 405 (wrong method), 413 (body too large), 415 (unsupported content type) and 500 (unhandled exception). Those are registered as one general handler rather than per-status cases, so a status nobody anticipated cannot slip back to HTML.

error.description: Stable class of failure. TICK-063 branches on this token, not on detail wording.

detail.description: Human-readable specifics, truncated to 256 characters so a rejected sidecar cannot inflate the response. Never the raw rejected input. Constrained by pattern rather than minLength because a whitespace-only string satisfies minLength and still renders as a blank, which is the same hole that was closed on the sidecar patterns in TICK-228 and TICK-229.

field.description: JSONPath of the offending sidecar field when validation failed. Absent when the failure is not a field error.
